How could you distinguish Pyrite from Chalcopyrite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Pyrite is harder (6-6.5, scratches glass) and pale brass-yellow; chalcopyrite is softer (3.5-4, scratched by a knife), deeper yellow and often iridescent.
keypoints: Pyrite is harder (6-6.5, scratches glass) and pale brass-yellow; chalcopyrite is softer (3.5-4, scratched by a knife), deeper yellow and often iridescent.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Pyrite from Gold in hand sample?
questions.answer: Gold is soft, malleable and very heavy (SG ~19) with a yellow streak; pyrite is hard, brittle and has a greenish-black streak.
keypoints: Gold is soft, malleable and very heavy (SG ~19) with a yellow streak; pyrite is hard, brittle and has a greenish-black streak.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Chalcopyrite from Gold in hand sample?
questions.answer: Gold has a yellow streak and is malleable; chalcopyrite has a greenish-black streak and is brittle.
keypoints: Gold has a yellow streak and is malleable; chalcopyrite has a greenish-black streak and is brittle.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Hematite from Magnetite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Hematite has a reddish-brown streak and is not (or only weakly) magnetic; magnetite has a black streak and is strongly magnetic.
keypoints: Hematite has a reddish-brown streak and is not (or only weakly) magnetic; magnetite has a black streak and is strongly magnetic.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Calcite from Rock Crystal in hand sample?
questions.answer: Calcite is hardness 3, has rhombohedral cleavage and fizzes in HCl; quartz is hardness 7 with conchoidal fracture and no fizz.
keypoints: Calcite is hardness 3, has rhombohedral cleavage and fizzes in HCl; quartz is hardness 7 with conchoidal fracture and no fizz.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Calcite from Dolomite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Calcite fizzes strongly in cold dilute HCl; dolomite fizzes only when powdered.
keypoints: Calcite fizzes strongly in cold dilute HCl; dolomite fizzes only when powdered.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Halite from Calcite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Halite tastes salty and has cubic cleavage (90°); calcite has rhombohedral cleavage and fizzes in acid.
keypoints: Halite tastes salty and has cubic cleavage (90°); calcite has rhombohedral cleavage and fizzes in acid.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Halite from Fluorite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Halite (H 2.5) has cubic cleavage and tastes salty; fluorite (H 4) has octahedral cleavage.
keypoints: Halite (H 2.5) has cubic cleavage and tastes salty; fluorite (H 4) has octahedral cleavage.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Muscovite from Biotite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Muscovite is colorless to silvery and potassium/aluminum-rich; biotite is black/brown because it contains iron and magnesium.
keypoints: Muscovite is colorless to silvery and potassium/aluminum-rich; biotite is black/brown because it contains iron and magnesium.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Orthoclase / Microcline from Albite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Plagioclase (albite) shows fine parallel striations from polysynthetic twinning; K-feldspar does not and is often pink.
keypoints: Plagioclase (albite) shows fine parallel striations from polysynthetic twinning; K-feldspar does not and is often pink.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Fluorapatite from Beryl in hand sample?
questions.answer: Both form hexagonal prisms, but apatite is hardness 5 (scratched by a knife) while beryl is 7.5-8.
keypoints: Both form hexagonal prisms, but apatite is hardness 5 (scratched by a knife) while beryl is 7.5-8.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Sodalite from Azurite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Sodalite has a white streak and does not fizz; azurite has a light blue streak and fizzes in HCl.
keypoints: Sodalite has a white streak and does not fizz; azurite has a light blue streak and fizzes in HCl.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Turquoise from Chrysocolla in hand sample?
questions.answer: Turquoise is harder (5-6); chrysocolla is softer (2-4) and lighter.
keypoints: Turquoise is harder (5-6); chrysocolla is softer (2-4) and lighter.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Galena from Stibnite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Galena forms cubes with cubic cleavage; stibnite forms long, striated, bladed prisms.
keypoints: Galena forms cubes with cubic cleavage; stibnite forms long, striated, bladed prisms.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Sphalerite from Galena in hand sample?
questions.answer: Sphalerite has a pale yellow-brown streak and resinous luster; galena has a lead-gray streak and metallic luster.
keypoints: Sphalerite has a pale yellow-brown streak and resinous luster; galena has a lead-gray streak and metallic luster.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Barite from Calcite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Barite is much denser (SG ~4.5 vs 2.7) and does not fizz in acid.
keypoints: Barite is much denser (SG ~4.5 vs 2.7) and does not fizz in acid.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Selenite from Muscovite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Both split into sheets, but selenite (gypsum) sheets are inelastic and it can be scratched by a fingernail; mica sheets spring back.
keypoints: Both split into sheets, but selenite (gypsum) sheets are inelastic and it can be scratched by a fingernail; mica sheets spring back.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Talc from Kaolinite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Talc feels soapy and is hardness 1; kaolinite is earthy and smells of clay when breathed on.
keypoints: Talc feels soapy and is hardness 1; kaolinite is earthy and smells of clay when breathed on.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Diamond from Rock Crystal in hand sample?
questions.answer: Diamond is hardness 10 with adamantine luster and octahedral cleavage; quartz is 7, vitreous, with conchoidal fracture.
keypoints: Diamond is hardness 10 with adamantine luster and octahedral cleavage; quartz is 7, vitreous, with conchoidal fracture.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Amethyst from Fluorite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Purple fluorite is hardness 4 with octahedral cleavage; amethyst is 7 with no cleavage.
keypoints: Purple fluorite is hardness 4 with octahedral cleavage; amethyst is 7 with no cleavage.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Olivine from Epidote in hand sample?
questions.answer: Olivine is olive green, granular, with no good cleavage, in mafic igneous rocks; epidote is pistachio green, striated, with one perfect cleavage, in metamorphic rocks.
keypoints: Olivine is olive green, granular, with no good cleavage, in mafic igneous rocks; epidote is pistachio green, striated, with one perfect cleavage, in metamorphic rocks.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Almandine from Grossular in hand sample?
questions.answer: Almandine is iron-aluminum garnet (deep red, schists); grossular is calcium-aluminum garnet (green/orange/yellow, skarns).
keypoints: Almandine is iron-aluminum garnet (deep red, schists); grossular is calcium-aluminum garnet (green/orange/yellow, skarns).

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Rhodochrosite from Rhodonite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Rhodochrosite is a carbonate (hardness 3.5-4, fizzes in warm HCl); rhodonite is a silicate (5.5-6.5) with black manganese-oxide veins.
keypoints: Rhodochrosite is a carbonate (hardness 3.5-4, fizzes in warm HCl); rhodonite is a silicate (5.5-6.5) with black manganese-oxide veins.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Azurite from Malachite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Azurite is deep blue; malachite is green and banded. Both are copper carbonates that fizz.
keypoints: Azurite is deep blue; malachite is green and banded. Both are copper carbonates that fizz.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Hornblende from Augite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Hornblende (amphibole) cleaves at 56°/124° and forms long six-sided prisms; augite (pyroxene) cleaves near 90° and forms stubby eight-sided prisms.
keypoints: Hornblende (amphibole) cleaves at 56°/124° and forms long six-sided prisms; augite (pyroxene) cleaves near 90° and forms stubby eight-sided prisms.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Milky Quartz from Albite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Milky quartz has no cleavage (conchoidal fracture); albite has two cleavages with striations.
keypoints: Milky quartz has no cleavage (conchoidal fracture); albite has two cleavages with striations.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Graphite from Pyrolusite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Both are black and soil fingers, but graphite is greasy and conducts electricity; pyrolusite is manganese oxide with a sooty feel and forms dendrites.
keypoints: Both are black and soil fingers, but graphite is greasy and conducts electricity; pyrolusite is manganese oxide with a sooty feel and forms dendrites.

questions.prompt: How could you distinguish Goethite / Limonite from Hematite in hand sample?
questions.answer: Goethite/limonite has a yellow-brown streak; hematite has a reddish-brown streak.
keypoints: Goethite/limonite has a yellow-brown streak; hematite has a reddish-brown streak.

questions.prompt: If olivine forms first as any magma cools, why is olivine rarely found in granite?
